s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic scalp lesions with disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages
salient_findings: Nonhealing crusted scalp lesions for 3 years
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages on the scalp
Yellowish crusts on the scalp
Osteolytic lesions on the right frontoparietal skull
Subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei on biopsy
key_facts: 4-year-old boy
3-year history of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions
Previous treatments with topical glucocorticosteroids and antibiotics showed no improvement
Occasional otitis media
Negative family history for skin disease
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages on the scalp
Yellowish crusts on the scalp
Normal routine blood examinations
Osteolytic lesions on the right frontoparietal skull on whole-body MRI
Subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei on punch biopsy of scalp
Infiltrate stained positively for CD1A on immunohistochemical staining
Normal ultrasonography of abdomen and lymph nodes
Normal serum electrophoresis

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive CD1A staining and presence of osteolytic lesions

shortlist.label: Indeterminate cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and subepidermal infiltrate with large cells

shortlist.label: Non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and histopathological findings consistent with non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of osteolytic lesions and subepidermal infiltrate

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and histopathological findings consistent with Rosai-Dorfman disease

shortlist.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and histopathological findings consistent with juvenile xanthogranuloma

shortlist.label: Histiocytoid Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and histopathological findings consistent with histiocytoid Sweet syndrome

shortlist.label: Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and histopathological findings consistent with multicentric reticulohistiocytosis

raw.rationale: The presence of osteolytic lesions, subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei, and positive staining for CD1A on immunohistochemical staining are characteristic findings of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Indeterminate cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Lack of specific markers and less typical clinical presentation

rejected.label: Non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Negative family history and absence of other typical features

rejected.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with adult onset and more systemic involvement

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: Characterized by massive lymphadenopathy, which is not present in this case

rejected.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: Typically presents with yellowish nodules and lacks the specific histiocytic markers

rejected.label: Histiocytoid Sweet syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by acute onset and lack of osteolytic lesions

rejected.label: Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with more widespread skin and joint involvement
